situation:
You are the client services manager at MERIDIAN LINE STAFFING, a staffing agency that places office and light industrial workers for employers across the region. The chief operating officer (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should spend its one-time expansion budget as it opens its first office outside the state.

MERIDIAN LINE leads its home market and has never operated outside it. Recruiters who resigned over the past two years said the same thing on the way out: they enter every candidate submission by hand and answer client email one message at a time, and the work leaves them no room to place people. The pattern sat in the files and nothing changed.

The budget covers one of two things. A placement and client-email system would automate the submissions and the routine client messages for both offices. It is priced against the volume the new office is forecast to carry by its first year, and that forecast rests on one large regional client that has shown interest and has not signed.

If that client signs, the system pays for itself and the pattern in the exit interviews ends. If the client does not sign, the money is spent and the home office carries a system sized for volume it does not have. Hiring recruiters and a client-relations person for the new office instead protects response times for existing clients and leaves the manual process, and the resignations it causes, exactly where they are.

The chief operating officer (judge) wants your recommendation on where the budget should go and what the company owes its existing clients while the new office opens. The chief operating officer (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the chief operating officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:

You have asked the client services manager to recommend whether the one-time expansion budget should buy the placement and client-email system or fund recruiters and a client-relations person for the new office, and to say what the company owes its existing clients while the office opens.

judgeQuestions: What would we be giving up by choosing the other way?
